column1: # catalog/test-tiers.tsv — which tier each suite runs in. Read by bin/test-tiers.sh
# (see its header); bin/ci-plan.sh applies it to the merge-queue batch and to the
# nightly run (.github/workflows/harness-nightly.yml). A suite with NO row is
# batch, and so is any row the reader cannot make sense of — the file can only
# ever move a suite OUT of the batch by saying so here, in review.
# Columns (tab separated): suite, tier, runtime_s, paths, reason
#   runtime_s  the suite's median wall time in a traced batch shard when it was
#              tiered (the 2026-09-28 test-value pass: 35 sampled batch runs,
#   paths      guard rows only: what a batch diff must touch for the guard to
#              run in the batch (exact file, dir/, or a glob); `-` otherwise
# THE NIGHTLY ROWS are the test-value report's SLOW-NEVER-FAILED bucket: >=10 s
# in a traced shard and 0 failures in the 35 sampled batch runs. Together they
# are ~41 of every batch's ~100 corpus suite-minutes. Before tiering one more,
# say what its runs show; to bring one back into every batch, delete its row.
# NEVER NIGHTLY, whatever their runtime (review of #3262):
#   * a suite bin/test-impact.sh runs on EVERY diff (`always`: it reads the
#     whole tree, so no PR "reaches" it and no builder gate runs it early) —
#   * a ratchet-shaped suite (a count, ceiling or pin over the live tree): it
#     must block the merge that breaks it, not a night later;
#   * a merge, approval, spend or brake safety suite;
#   * the switch-* ratchet family (another change is rewriting it).
# THE GUARD ROWS are safety and leak guards: a nightly miss on them costs more
# than a slow batch, so a batch that touches what they guard still runs them.
